This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Sr Director Software Engineer based in United States.

This is a senior technology leadership opportunity focused on building and scaling software platforms that support clinical genomic diagnostics.

You will lead a high-performing software engineering organization spanning bioinformatics, data platforms, workflow automation, and production systems.

The role combines strategic ownership with strong technical oversight, shaping architecture, engineering standards, roadmaps, and delivery priorities.

You will work closely with scientific, clinical, quality, operations, product, and executive stakeholders to translate complex requirements into reliable software solutions.

A key focus will be modernizing legacy platforms and transitioning research innovations into validated, production-ready workflows.

You will also champion responsible AI adoption, automation, observability, and engineering practices that improve quality, efficiency, and scalability.

This is an opportunity to influence technology strategy in a mission-driven, regulated environment where software directly supports advanced genomic diagnostics.

Accountabilities

Define and own the software engineering vision, technical roadmap, delivery priorities, operating model, resource plans, and engineering standards for a bioinformatics software engineering organization.
Lead, mentor, hire, and develop software engineers, bioinformatics engineers, technical leads, and managers while fostering accountability, collaboration, technical excellence, and continuous improvement.
Oversee the architecture, development, implementation, maintenance, and operational support of production-grade software platforms, bioinformatics workflows, data systems, and reporting solutions.
Drive modernization initiatives involving legacy systems, workflow orchestration, automation, containerization, cloud and HPC computing, data integration, APIs, and scalable software architectures.
Establish strong production operations practices, including monitoring, observability, incident response, escalation processes, root-cause analysis, post-release support, and reliability improvements.
Partner with R&D, clinical laboratory, quality, operations, product, data, and executive stakeholders to translate scientific, clinical, and business priorities into actionable software roadmaps.
Lead prioritization, scope definition, dependency management, resource planning, delivery governance, and executive communication across complex software initiatives.
Guide research algorithms, analytical prototypes, scripts, and proof-of-concept tools through the transition into scalable, tested, validated, documented, and maintainable production workflows.
Establish and enforce software development lifecycle standards covering requirements, architecture reviews, code reviews, automated testing, CI/CD, validation, documentation, release management, and change control.
Ensure software practices meet applicable quality, regulatory, privacy, security, traceability, and audit-readiness expectations within clinical diagnostics and other regulated environments.
Define and monitor engineering KPIs covering roadmap delivery, system reliability, software quality, technical debt, production incidents, team health, stakeholder satisfaction, and operational efficiency.
Lead responsible adoption of AI-enabled engineering, workflow automation, documentation, decision-support, code assistance, issue triage, and operational capabilities, with appropriate governance and human oversight.
Reduce technical debt and improve scalability, maintainability, performance, deployment efficiency, automation, documentation, and integration across critical platforms and workflows.
Evaluate technology investments, build-versus-buy decisions, architecture patterns, and emerging technologies to ensure long-term alignment with organizational strategy.
Communicate technical decisions, risks, tradeoffs, roadmap progress, and recommendations effectively to executive, technical, scientific, clinical, quality, and business audiences.

Requirements

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Bioinformatics, Computational Biology, Genomics, Data Science, or another relevant technical or quantitative field.
12+ years of experience in software engineering, bioinformatics software development, clinical genomics technology, data platforms, or related computational technology disciplines.
7+ years of software engineering leadership experience, including people management, hiring, performance management, mentoring, organizational planning, and leadership of technical leads or managers.
Demonstrated success defining engineering strategy, technical roadmaps, delivery priorities, resource plans, and operating models for complex software organizations or platforms.
Proven experience leading production-grade software systems, bioinformatics workflows, data platforms, workflow automation, or reporting applications in clinical, healthcare, laboratory, or regulated environments.
Strong expertise in software architecture, system design, APIs, data integration, database-backed applications, workflow orchestration, scalable computing, and modern software development practices.
Experience establishing or improving engineering standards covering requirements management, code review, automated testing, CI/CD, validation, documentation, release management, incident management, and production support.
Practical understanding of NGS data, clinical genomics workflows, bioinformatics pipelines, genomic data formats, variant analysis, laboratory interfaces, or diagnostic reporting systems.
Experience transforming research prototypes, analytical methods, scripts, or proof-of-concept solutions into scalable, validated, documented, and maintainable production workflows.
Experience operating within quality, regulatory, privacy, security, traceability, and audit-readiness frameworks relevant to clinical diagnostics, healthcare technology, laboratory operations, or regulated software.
Strong technical fluency with Git-based development, automated testing, CI/CD, Linux, containers, workflow orchestration, cloud or HPC computing, databases, APIs, and monitoring or observability tools.
Experience with technologies such as Nextflow, Docker, Kubernetes, cloud platforms, microservices, API-driven architectures, data lakes, data warehouses, and enterprise data integration is highly valuable.
Familiarity with AI-enabled engineering tools, large language models, agentic AI, automation, decision-support systems, or AI-assisted operational workflows is preferred.
Master’s degree or PhD in a relevant technical field is preferred.
Experience with CAP/CLIA-regulated laboratory environments, molecular diagnostics, clinical genomics, variant interpretation, healthcare interoperability, or related domains is a strong advantage.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate complex technical and scientific concepts for diverse stakeholders.
Strong judgment, analytical thinking, problem-solving ability, and a practical approach to balancing quality, delivery, scalability, and business priorities.
Demonstrated ability to collaborate effectively with scientists, engineers, clinical teams, laboratory personnel, quality professionals, and senior business leaders.
Commitment to reproducibility, documentation, automation, maintainability, operational excellence, and high-quality engineering practices.

Benefits

Salary: Competitive compensation package based on experience, qualifications, and role requirements.
Work arrangement: Fully remote position based in the United States.
Opportunity to lead technology strategy for software platforms supporting clinical genomic diagnostics and scientific innovation.
Senior-level ownership of engineering architecture, organizational development, modernization, and delivery strategy.
Opportunity to work cross-functionally with software engineering, bioinformatics, R&D, clinical laboratory, quality, operations, product, and executive teams.
Professional growth through leadership of experienced engineering teams and exposure to advanced genomics, regulated technology, cloud/HPC platforms, and AI-enabled engineering.

jobs.title: VP of Engineering, Storage Protocols
jobs.description:
Own Every Moment at NetApp

At NetApp, your ideas power innovation. We lead in intelligent data infrastructure—delivering unified storage, integrated data services, and solutions that help organizations unlock the full potential of their data, from AI to multicloud.

Ready to innovate and contribute to our path to $10B? Here, you'll collaborate with passionate teams, tackle real-world challenges, and see your impact in how customers transform and grow. If you're ready to bring curiosity, creativity, and drive to every moment, NetApp is where your journey begins. Join teams that innovate to elevate, drive results, and excel together across every function.

Job Summary

VP of Engineering, Storage Protocols

The Opportunity

Storage is having its moment again — AI training and inference workloads are forcing a rethink of how data is stored, moved, and served at scale, and NetApp sits at the center of that shift. As VP of Engineering for Storage Protocols, you'll own the technical strategy and execution for File (NAS), Block (SAN), and Object (S3) across ONTAP and StorageGRID. Your central mandate is guiding these teams to meet the performance, quality, and scale demands that AI workloads are placing on the protocol stack — from high-concurrency training-data access to inference-time latency and reliability at scale — while keeping the enterprise workloads that are our foundation running without compromise.

This is a build-and-lead role for someone who wants deep technical ownership at VP scope: real architectural authority, a seat in executive strategy discussions, and a mandate to shape how NetApp's protocol stack evolves to meet the next generation of workloads.

Role:

Reports to: SVP of Platform Engineering

Location: Remote-friendly — we're flexible on where you're based. Our senior leadership team is primarily based in San Jose, CA, and this role should expect to spend meaningful time there.

Scope: Leads engineering across File, Block, Object, and StorageGRID protocol teams — an organization of roughly 350 engineers.

Job Requirements

What You'll Own

Technical strategy and execution across ONTAP's File (NFS, SMB, multiprotocol), Block (iSCSI, FC, NVMe/TCP, NVMe/FC), and Object (S3) protocol teams, plus the StorageGRID engineering organization.
The architectural roadmap for object storage across the portfolio — including how performance-oriented ONTAP S3 and capacity/throughput-oriented StorageGRID object storage differentiate and integrate — partnering closely with Product Management so engineering investment stays coherent rather than duplicative.
The technical roadmap for multiprotocol data access that balances enterprise workload modernization with emerging AI/ML training, inference, and data-lakehouse use cases.
Reliability, performance, and scale for the protocol stack, including executive-level ownership of major customer escalations involving protocol behavior at scale.
Standards participation and protocol compliance (NFS, SMB, iSCSI, FC, NVMe, S3, tables) to keep NetApp interoperable across enterprise and hyperscaler ecosystems.
Organizational design for where protocol and control-plane capabilities sit within Platform Engineering — grounded in evidence like backlog composition and ownership boundaries.
Building and retaining a high-performing, multi-layered engineering leadership team across File, Block, Object, and StorageGRID.
Close partnership with peer engineering leaders across ONTAP Core, Manageability, and Data Replication (MetroCluster, SnapMirror) to keep the broader storage platform architecturally coherent.
A voice in executive technical strategy, including NetApp's technical narrative on object and metadata architecture for neocloud customers.

Required

What We're Looking For

15+ years of engineering leadership in storage, infrastructure, or platform software, including 8+ years leading multiple layers of engineering management.
Deep technical fluency in enterprise distributed systems — e.g., storage protocols (NAS, block, or object/S3), large-scale networking, or comparable infrastructure domains — with the ability to go deep on at least one and reason credibly across the others.
A track record of resolving ambiguous, cross-organizational architectural and org-design questions, and of leading large-scale customer escalations to resolution across engineering, support, and field teams.
Excellent executive communication — you can represent complex technical tradeoffs clearly to senior leadership and partner effectively with Product Management.

Strongly Preferred

Experience building storage or data infrastructure for AI/ML workloads — training, inference, or data pipelines.
Experience restructuring or right-sizing engineering teams based on evidence rather than assumption.
A leadership style grounded in developing others, not positional authority.

Education

Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related field.

Compensation:

The target salary range for this position is 323,000 - 418,000 USD. The salary offered will be determined by the candidate's location, qualifications, experience, and education and may be outside of this range. Final compensation packages are competitive and in line with industry standards, reflecting a variety of factors, and include a comprehensive benefits package. This may cover Health Insurance, Life Insurance, Retirement or Pension Plans, Paid Time Off, various Leave options, Performance-Based Incentives, employee stock purchase plan, and/or restricted stocks (RSU’s), with all offerings subject to regional variations and governed by local laws, regulations, and company policies. Benefits may vary by country and region, and further details will be provided as part of the recruitment process.

At NetApp, we embrace a hybrid working environment designed to strengthen connection, collaboration, and culture for all employees. This means that most roles will have some level of in-office and/or in-person expectations, which will be shared during the recruitment process.

jobs.title: Director, Corporate Engineering
jobs.description:
I. Job Summary

The Director, Corporate Engineering provides strategic and operational leadership for the company's engineering function across landfill operations, renewable energy assets, and environmental compliance initiatives. This role is responsible for developing engineering standards, leading capital project planning, driving operational excellence, and ensuring engineering activities support the company's safety, sustainability, regulatory, and financial objectives.

The Director partners closely with Operations, Environmental Compliance, Sustainability, Renewable Energy, Fleet, Finance, Procurement, Legal and senior leadership teams to deliver complex capital projects, improve asset reliability, optimize operating performance, and support long-term business growth.

II. Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Management of the monthly processes associated with Landfill Capital projects submitted for review at WM investment committee meetings.
Management of WM’s annual Engineer Training Program including involvement in recruiting, hiring and program management each year.
Responsible for technical support (individual or with appropriate Engineering team personnel) as needed for WM’s Enterprise Risk programs as well as WM’s Wastewater Solutions team.
Responsible for the P&L of the corporate Engineering Team department including SG&A personnel/expenses as well as Disposal Operations personnel/expenses with a total annual budget of approximately $3.5M+.
Management of a 10+ person team including the following responsibilities:
Budgeting the annual LF Capital and Final Capping as well as monthly forecasting of LF Capital and Final Capping.
Processes associated with WM’s annual LF Workbook program as well as annual Engineering team reviews of LF Workbooks received from WM Area personnel.
Environmental, compliance and property condition due diligence reviews of WM acquisitions.
WM’s corporate CAD team including airspace policies and procedures, annual airspace report preparation procedures/processes, and annual overfill certification requirements and documentation.
Development and management of WM’s Reality Capture, DroneDeploy and AutoDesk Construction Cloud (ACC) platforms and processes
Implementation of GHG emission strategies at an enterprise level including support for WM Scenario Planning Tool, GHG Capital budgeting and tracking, as well as risk and opportunity management associated with reduction of emissions from WM Landfill facilities.

Responsible for the planning, development, implementation and execution of strategies associated with data analytics, process improvement, long term capital planning and the modernization of the current financial planning process.
Responsible for go forward strategies associated with the development of AUF improvement analytics as well as facility fill sequence plans to continue to implement “Plan the Work and Work the Plan” processes as part of the implement of WM’s Reality Capture platform.

III. Qualifications

The requirements listed below are representative of the qualifications necessary to perform the job. Must live and work in the US.

Required

Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Civil Engineering, Environmental Engineering, Chemical Engineering, or related discipline.
10+ years of progressive engineering leadership experience focused on solid waste and landfills.
Experience managing large-scale capital projects and engineering teams.
Strong knowledge of engineering design, construction, asset management, and project execution.
Demonstrated success partnering with operations and executive leadership teams.
Strong financial, analytical, and project management skills.
Excellent communication and stakeholder management capabilities.

Preferred

Professional Engineer (PE) license.
Master's degree in Engineering, Business Administration, or related field.
Experience within environmental services, waste management, recycling, renewable energy, industrial infrastructure, or heavy operations.
Familiarity with landfill operations, transfer stations, MRFs, RNG, or environmental compliance requirements.

IV. Physical Requirements

Listed below are key points regarding physical demands, physical and occupational risks, and the work environment of the job. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the job.

Required to use motor coordination with finger dexterity (such as keyboarding, machine operation, etc.) most of the work day;
Required to exert physical effort in handling objects less than 30 pounds rarely;
Required to be exposed to physical occupational risks (such as cuts, burns, exposure to toxic chemicals, etc.) occasionally;
Required to be exposed to physical environment which involves dirt, odors, noise, weather extremes or similar elements occasionally;
Normal setting for this job is in an office.

‌Pay: The expected base pay range for this position across the U.S. is $152000 - $218000. This range represents a good faith estimate for this position. The specific salary offered to a successful candidate may be influenced by a variety of factors including the candidate’s relevant experience, education, training, certifications, qualifications, and work location

V. Benefits

At WM, each eligible employee receives a competitive total compensation package that includes medical, dental, vision, life insurance, and short-term disability. In addition, we offer a stock purchase plan, company matching on a 401(k), and more. Employees also receive paid vacation, holidays, and personal days. Please note that benefits may vary by site.

If this sounds like the opportunity that you have been looking for, please click Apply.

jobs.title: Senior Engineering Manager, Data Engineering
jobs.description:
Omada Health is on a mission to bend the curve of chronic disease.
Job overview: 

Our Data Engineering team builds and operates the data platform and curated data products that power analytics, reporting, experimentation, and AI-driven insights across Product, Clinical, Commercial, Finance, and Operations. We are looking for an experienced Senior Engineering Manager, Data Engineering
to lead our data engineering organization and help shape the future of Omada's enterprise data platform.
As a Senior Engineering Manager, you will lead a team responsible for designing, building, and operating scalable data pipelines that serve as the trusted foundation for business intelligence, machine learning features, product analytics, operational reporting, experimentation, and advanced analytics.
You will partner closely with Data Architects, Product Managers, Analytics, Data Science, Governance, and Software Engineering teams to define the technical strategy, execution roadmap, and operating model for Data Engineering.
This role requires a strong balance of organizational leadership and technical depth. You will build high-performing engineering teams, drive platform strategy, and deliver reliable, scalable, and governed data capabilities that enable data-driven decision making across Omada.
Key Responsibilities:

Establish and execute a strategic roadmap for Omada's Data Engineering platform.
Lead the delivery of scalable, reliable, and governed data products that enable analytics, reporting, experimentation, and AI-driven insights.
Deliver trusted, reusable production datasets that power Applied Data Science, Product, Clinical, Commercial, Finance, Operations, and Executive analytics.
Lead, develop and grow a high-performing Data Engineering organization through hiring, coaching, mentoring, and career development.
Foster a culture of technical excellence, collaboration, accountability, and continuous learning.
Empower teams to deliver high-impact solutions while maintaining a strong focus on quality and operational excellence.
Partner with Product, Analytics, Data Science, Architecture, Governance, and Engineering leaders to define priorities and accelerate data-driven decision making across Omada.
Translate business needs into scalable platform capabilities and trusted data products.
Build strong relationships across the organization to drive alignment, transparency, and execution.
Establish engineering excellence through improved data quality, reliability, observability, security, and platform performance.
Define and monitor engineering and operational metrics to continuously improve platform health, cost efficiency, and developer productivity.
Guide adoption of Improved reliability, quality, governance, and usability of enterprise data products.
Provide technical leadership for architecture, platform evolution, scalable technologies, reusable frameworks, and engineering standards across Data Engineering.
Expand self-service analytics through trusted and reusable data capabilities.
Influence long-term technology strategy while partnering with engineering leaders across Omada to build a world-class data platform.

About you: 

Experience:

10+ years of experience building and operating large-scale data platforms, analytics systems, or software platforms.
5+ years of experience leading Data Engineering teams, with experience managing managers or multiple teams preferred.
Proven ability to build, mentor, and scale high-performing engineering organizations.
Demonstrated success defining technical strategy, driving execution, and delivering complex cross-functional initiatives.
Strong experience partnering with Product, Analytics, Data Science, and executive stakeholders.
Deep experience designing and operating modern cloud-based analytics platforms, including data warehouses, lakehouses, ELT/ETL pipelines, and data processing systems.
Strong understanding of data modeling, analytics architecture, semantic layers, and scalable data product design.
Experience implementing data quality, observability, governance, metadata, lineage, and access control capabilities.
Experience modernizing enterprise data platforms and driving adoption of modern data engineering practices.
Familiarity with AI and machine learning data workflows is a plus.

Technical Skills:

Strong understanding of distributed data systems, cloud-native architectures, and software engineering practices.
Experience with modern data technologies such as Databricks, Spark, Airflow, Kafka, Redshift, Snowflake, Python, SQL, Graph DB and AWS.
Experience with CI/CD, infrastructure automation, testing frameworks, monitoring, and performance optimization.
Familiarity with modern data governance platforms such as Unity Catalog, Collibra, or OpenMetadata is a plus.

Communication Skills:

Exceptional leadership, communication, and stakeholder management skills.
Ability to influence technical direction across multiple engineering teams and organizational boundaries.
Passion for mentoring engineers and developing future technical leaders.
Ability to balance immediate business needs with long-term platform investments.
Comfortable operating in ambiguous environments and creating clarity, alignment, and execution.

Education:
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science or a similar discipline preferred.
Technologies we use:
Ruby on Rails, Redshift, Athena, Postgres, SQL, Python, Apache Airflow, Appflow, S3, SNS, SQS, Kafka, Docker, Kubernetes, AWS infrastructure, Lambda, Serverless, Tableau, Datadog, GitLabCI, Cursor, OpenMetadata, Databricks
Bonus Points for:

Experience building data pipelines for Healthcare or highly governed industries is a big plus.

Benefits:

Competitive salary with generous annual cash bonus
Equity grants
Remote first work from home culture
Flexible Time Off to help you rest, recharge, and connect with loved ones
Generous parental leave
Health, dental, and vision insurance (and above market employer contributions)
401k retirement savings plan
Lifestyle Spending Account (LSA)
Mental Health Support Solutions
...and more!

It takes a village to change health care. As we build together toward our mission, we strive to embody the following values in our day-to-day work. We hope these hold meaning for you as well as you consider Omada!
Cultivate Trust.

We listen closely and we operate with kindness. We provide respectful and candid feedback to each other.
Seek Context.

We ask to understand and we build connections. We do our research up front to move faster down the road.
Act Boldly.

We innovate daily to solve problems, improve processes, and find new opportunities for our members and customers.
Deliver Results.

We reward impact above output. We set a high bar, we’re not afraid to fail, and we take pride in our work.
Succeed Together.

We prioritize Omada’s progress above team or individual. We have fun as we get stuff done, and we celebrate together. 
Remember Why We’re Here.

We push through the challenges of changing health care because we know the destination is worth it.

About Omada Health:
Omada Health (Nasdaq: OMDA) is reverse engineering the way healthcare is delivered in America, putting the space between doctor visits–where health is won or lost–at the center of care. Today's healthcare system poorly serves chronic conditions that require ongoing support outside of the exam room, like obesity, diabetes, hypertension, cholesterol, and musculoskeletal conditions. Omada’s virtual-first model combines human-led care teams, connected devices, and AI-enabled technology to deliver personalized care at scale, including support for GLP-1 therapy. Omada has served more than two million members since launch across 2,000+ employers, health plans, pharmacy benefit managers, and health systems. Learn more at omadahealth.com.
Omada is thrilled to share that we’ve been certified as a Great Place to Work! Please click here for more information.
We carefully hire the best talent we can find, which means actively seeking diversity of beliefs, backgrounds, education, and ways of thinking. We strive to build an inclusive culture where differences are celebrated and leveraged to inform better design and business decisions. Omada is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace and affirmative action employer. We are committed to equal opportunity regardless of race, color, religion, sex, gender identity, national origin, ancestry, citizenship, age, physical or mental disability, legally protected medical condition, family care status, military or veteran status, marital status, domestic partner status, sexual orientation, or any other basis protected by local, state, or federal laws.

*The actual offer, including the compensation package, will be within the posted range for the relevant zone and will be determined based on multiple factors, such as the candidate's skills and experience, and other business considerations such as internal equity.

jobs.title: Director of Data & Intelligence Engineering
jobs.description:
Description & Requirements

The Director of Data & Intelligence serves as a senior leader within the Analytics and Applied Intelligence (AAI) practice and is accountable for the Data Foundation layer (Layer 1) of the firm's agentic intelligence framework, including the semantic fabric, vector stores, knowledge graphs, MCP connectors, and Zero-ETL pipelines that power autonomous systems and Client Zero solutions. This leader provides strategic direction, mentorship, technical coaching, and people leadership to the firm's Data & Intelligence Engineers, including professionals transitioning from Backend Data Designer and Data Engineer roles. Operating as a peer and key collaborator to the senior leaders of the AI Solutions Architects and Intelligence Designers teams, this role partners closely on solution architecture, end-to-end agentic delivery, and the development of Center of Excellence standards. The position follows a flexible hybrid work model with approximately 10% travel and requires availability during Eastern Standard Time (EST) business hours. Due to project requirements, all professionals serving in this role must reside and perform all work within the United States. Candidates must be legally authorized to work in the United States now and in the future. Verification of employment eligibility will be required at the time of hire, and visa sponsorship is not available for this position.

What You Will Do

Lead the Data & Intelligence Engineering discipline across the AAI practice - setting technical direction, quality standards, and delivery patterns for the Layer 1 Data Foundation that supports delivery.

Provide coaching, career development, and performance feedback to Data & Intelligence Engineers.

Partner with peer leaders of the AI Solutions Architects and Intelligence Designers to define solution architecture, hand-offs across the three logic layers (Data, Reasoning, Validation), and shared standards for MCP, evals, and HITL.

Contribute to the AAI Center of Excellence (Hub) - selecting frontier tooling, codifying standards (Zero-ETL, vector DBs, knowledge graphs, MCP), and ensuring cross-team knowledge sharing.

Represent the practice on AI Ethics, model governance, data sovereignty, and responsible AI guardrails, in alignment with the AAI Steering Committee and Client Zero principles.

Architect and oversee the Data Foundation layer of agentic systems: vector stores (Pinecone, Weaviate, Milvus), knowledge graphs (Neo4j), semantic layers, and Zero-ETL / real-time streaming pipelines.

Thorough understanding of data modeling, relational, and non-relational principles; expert level SQL

Expertise in Python data engineering packages and patterns, including Python and PySpark

Familiarity and experience with the different data engineering platforms commonly used such as Fabric, Databricks, Snowflake, Synapse

Solid leadership-level fluency with cloud fundamentals (Azure preferred, GCP, AWS) and modern data architecture (lakehouse, data contracts, governance, lineage)

Expected to actively collaborate with clients and team members to meet project objectives and timelines; Strong communication skills (verbal and written) for executive, client, and team audiences.

Experience with building, testing and deploying data pipelines, ML/AI models; understanding of GenAI/Agentic AI use cases (experience strongly preferred)

Design and govern MCP (Model Context Protocol) connectors that securely expose enterprise sources (Jira, CRM, ERP, lakehouse) as tools consumable by agents and frontier models.

Set standards for Graph-RAG, RAG optimization, chunking strategy, and retrieval evaluation to minimize hallucinations and ensure high-quality context for downstream LLM components.

Partner with AI Solutions Architects to ensure data tools, semantic layers, and MCP services meet the needs of agentic workflows (LangChain, LangGraph, CrewAI) and frontier model integrations (GPT, Claude, Gemini).

Partner with Intelligence Designers to ensure data structures support HITL workflows, Action Centers, evals, and Golden Set testing.

Enforce row-/column-level security, federated identity (Entra ID / OAuth), and policy-as-code guardrails across all agent-accessible data.

Minimum Qualifications

BS in data science, computer science or other related fields (MS strongly preferred)

8+ years of relevant data engineering / data science experience, with demonstrated depth in modern data architecture (Zero-ETL, vector/graph databases, semantic layers, RAG)

7+ years of experience leading, coaching, and developing teams of professionals (typically 5-10+), including senior individual contributors; consulting environment strongly preferred.

Proven track record partnering with peer technical leaders (e.g., solutions architecture, UX/interface design) to deliver integrated, multidisciplinary platforms.

Demonstrated experience deploying RAG architectures and MCP-based integrations in production environments, including evaluation frameworks (evals, RAGAS, Golden Set testing) for probabilistic systems.

Familiarity with AI Ethics, responsible AI guardrails, and governance frameworks suitable for enterprise and regulated environments.

Preferred Qualifications

Prior experience in professional services or consulting, ideally leading a data engineering or applied AI practice area.

Experience translating client business problems into agentic data architectures (semantic layers, knowledge graphs, MCP tool design).

Hands-on exposure to LLM orchestration frameworks (LangChain, LangGraph, CrewAI) sufficient to coach engineers on integration patterns.

Experience with production agent monitoring, observability, SLA design, and incident response for probabilistic systems (in partnership with the Agent Operations Lead).

Forvis Mazars, LLP is an independent member of Forvis Mazars Global, a leading global professional services network. Ranked among the largest public accounting firms in the United States, our 7,000+ team members deliver assurance, tax, and consulting services to clients in all 50 states and internationally.

With a legacy spanning more than 100 years, we're building something different. We are guided by a shared promise: Together, we create extraordinary experiences. That means delivering an Unmatched Client Experience® while creating a workplace where relationships matter, learning fuels growth, and every person feels valued and supported to thrive.

Our robust total rewards program and flexible work environment reflect our commitment to people, careers, and well-being-empowering our team to grow and thrive while delivering exceptional service. To explore what makes working at Forvis Mazars special, visit www.forvismazars.us/careers.

jobs.title: Director, Global Solutions Engineering
jobs.description:
Who are we?

At UpGuard, we are replacing manual security bottlenecks with AI-driven precision. Fresh off a US$75M Series C, we are scaling our infrastructure to process 100 billion risk signals daily. This isn’t just growth; it’s a total reimagining of how the world manages cyber risk.

We build the Cyber Risk Posture Management (CRPM) platform that security teams actually love. By integrating security ratings, threat intel, and agentic AI, we empower organisations to stay ahead of an ever evolving attack surface.

We aren’t just building another tool; we’re defining a category. We provide the autonomy to ship world-class technology and the resources to do it at a global scale.

Why are we hiring for this role?

We're hiring a Director of Global Solutions Engineering
to lead the technical engine behind our revenue organization. As a cybersecurity company, our technical credibility is central to how we win and keep customers — and this leader owns it across the customer journey. You'll run a global, two-part function as a manager of managers: Sales Engineers
who drive the technical win in new business (pre-sales), and Solutions Consultants
who serve as the technical escalation path for our post-sales teams. You'll report directly to the CRO.

This is a builder's role for a leader who is equally comfortable in a strategy conversation with the executive team, in a technical deep-dive with an engineer, and jumping into a live customer call to lead it when it counts. Details of the remit are below.

What will you do?

Lead a global, multi-layered team. Manage and develop distributed managers and their teams of Sales Engineers and Solutions Consultants across regions. Hire, coach, and retain top technical talent; set clear career paths; and build a culture of technical excellence, curiosity, and customer obsession.
Own the technical win in pre-sales. Lead the Sales Engineering team to drive pipeline conversion through world-class demos, proofs of concept, technical discovery, and value engineering — consistently earning the technical decision.
Own the post-sales technical escalation path. Lead the Solutions Consultants team as the technical escalation path for CSMs and the driver of technical cross-sell across our product suite. (Note: with a dedicated Professional Services team being stood up, Solutions Consultants are not expected to own customer onboarding today — though this scope may evolve.)
Stay hands-on when it counts. Be willing and able to personally jump into a high-stakes customer call and lead it — you set the technical bar by example, not just from the org chart.
Elevate RFPs and security assessments. Build a scalable, high-quality function for RFPs, security questionnaires, and technical/security assessments — improving accuracy, consistency, and turnaround, and building reusable content that raises win rates.
Enable and scale the channel. Technically enable partners — training, certification, demo readiness, and deal support — so they can independently represent and implement our product.
Partner with Enablement. Work with Sales Enablement to design and deliver technical training, certification, demo standards, and competitive playbooks that keep the team and the wider revenue org sharp.
Be the voice of the customer to Product. Capture field and technical feedback and channel it to Product and Engineering to influence the roadmap.
Operate as a revenue leader. Contribute to forecasting, capacity planning, and go-to-market strategy with the CRO and revenue leadership team, and define the metrics and processes that make the function measurable and scalable.

What will you bring?

We care far more about your track record than your tenure. The bar is a leader who has built and run a world-class technical team serving technical customers with a technical product.
A demonstrated track record of building and leading a world-class Solutions/Sales Engineering team — you've raised the technical bar of an organization, not just managed headcount.
Experience selling and supporting a genuinely technical product to technical buyers and evaluators (engineers, security teams, architects). Cybersecurity or security/GRC experience is strongly preferred; adjacent deeply-technical domains considered.
Proven experience as a manager of managers leading distributed or global teams across multiple time zones.
Ownership of the technical experience across the customer journey — from the technical win in new business through post-sales technical support and cross-sell.

jobs.title: DIRECTOR OF RESEARCH TECHNOLOGY SERVICES
jobs.description:
DIRECTOR OF RESEARCH TECHNOLOGY SERVICES

JOB SUMMARY
Under the general direction of the Chief Information Officer, provides executive, technical, and operational leadership for technology services supporting the University’s research enterprise within Information Technology Services (ITS). The Director is responsible for developing and implementing solutions, policies, and services that advance the University’s research mission through effective use of technology. The Director serves as the primary liaison between ITS, the Office of the Vice President for Research (OVPR), faculty researchers, research centers, and other stakeholders to ensure that technology services effectively support current and emerging research needs and has a dotted line reporting relationship to the Vice President for Research, Innovation and Entrepreneurship.
The Director provides leadership for research computing services, secure research environments, research data services, research cybersecurity initiatives, compliance-driven research technologies, artificial intelligence and emerging research technologies, and strategic research technology planning. The Director works collaboratively with all ITS teams to coordinate the delivery of research technology services across the University. The Director also works with peers at UConn Health’s to help meet the needs of researchers across UConn and UConn Health through a shared information technology resources model.
For activities related to these responsibilities, the Director interacts and coordinates with University administration, OVPR leadership, faculty researchers, campus and department technology leaders, research centers and institutes, technology advisory groups, external partners, and individual members of the University community across UConn and UConn Health. The Director serves as an advisor to the CIO and other University leaders on research technology, governance, and secure service delivery. The Director coordinates and participates in high-level technology assessments, program planning, and serves as a member of the ITS Leadership Team.
The Director maintains budgets and staffing levels appropriate to assigned responsibilities, oversees personnel planning, hiring, and assessment, attends conferences and professional development activities, and interacts with external peers to maintain knowledge of current issues, opportunities, and best practices in research technology services.
DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
• Provides leadership and direction to the University on research technology services, research computing, secure research environments, research data management, research cybersecurity, and emerging technologies supporting the University’s research mission and priorities
• Develops and maintains a long-term strategic vision and roadmap for research technology services in partnership with University leadership, OVPR, faculty researchers, and ITS leadership.
• Serves as the primary relationship manager between ITS and the research community, ensuring that researcher needs, priorities, and challenges are understood and addressed through effective technology solutions and services.
• Establishes and maintains strong partnerships with faculty, research centers, OVPR leadership, and external stakeholders to identify opportunities, improve service delivery, and advance research initiatives.
• Oversees the portfolio of research technology initiatives and projects, ensuring effective planning, communication, risk management, prioritization, resource coordination, and successful service delivery.
• Provides technical leadership and coordination for secure research computing initiatives supporting regulated research activities, including environments requiring compliance with NIST 800-171, CMMC, HIPAA, and other applicable regulatory frameworks.
• Works collaboratively with ITS infrastructure, security, networking, enterprise systems, cloud services, and application teams to ensure research technology services are aligned with University standards, policies, and strategic objectives.
• Provides technical leadership and coordination for research computing resources, cloud-based research environments, research data services, and advanced computing capabilities .
• Identifies opportunities to leverage emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence, advanced analytics, cloud computing, and research data platforms, to support the University's research enterprise.
• Oversees staffing, hiring, training, mentoring, performance evaluation, and discipline for assigned employees and serves as the departmental representative for all union-related issues.
• Develops and maintains budgets associated with research technology services and provides guidance regarding technology investments, contracts, software licensing, cloud services, and vendor relationships.
• Establishes service metrics and performance measures to evaluate effectiveness, improve service quality, and ensure alignment with institutional goals and researcher needs.
• Prepares periodic reports regarding strategic initiatives, project portfolios, operational activities, budgets, service performance, and emerging opportunities.
• Interacts with ITS senior leadership, University governance groups, technology planning committees, and IT leaders across th UConn and UConn Health to ensure coordination and alignment of research technology initiatives.
• Performs other duties as required.
MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS
• Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution.
• Minimum of ten (10) years of progressively responsible experience in information technology, research computing, research technology services, or a related field.
• Minimum of five (5) years of higher education experience in a research-intensive university or comparable research environment.
• Experience supporting technology services for faculty researchers and research programs.
• Experience with research computing, secure research environments, research data services, cloud technologies, or related research technology disciplines.
• Experience working with compliance requirements related to research, including NIST 800-171, CMMC, HIPAA, FERPA, or other applicable frameworks.
• Excellent and demonstrated project and portfolio management skills, including strategic planning, prioritization, resource coordination, budget management, and successful delivery of complex initiatives.
• Strong personnel supervision skills, including employee performance management, mentoring, communication, team development, and organizational leadership.
• Demonstrated ability to build partnerships and maintain productive relationships with faculty, researchers, administrators, and technology professionals.
• Demonstrated ability to act decisively and solve problems through creative, collaborative, and strategic thinking.
• Ability to identify key issues in complex situations, evaluate alternatives, and develop effective strategies for resolution.
• Ability to translate strategic objectives into operational plans and align resources with institutional priorities.
• Proven leadership, communication, and relationship-building skills with diverse university constituencies.
• Ability to build effective teams that emphasize service, partnership, collaboration, accountability, and continuous improvement.
PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS
• Advanced degree from an accredited institution.
• Experience in a leadership role supporting research technology services within a major research university.
• Experience collaborating with offices supporting research administration, compliance, sponsored programs, or research security.
• Relevant certifications related to project management, information security, cloud technologies, research administration, or technology leadership.
• Experience developing technology governance structures and stakeholder engagement programs.
APPOINTMENT TERMS
This is a full-time, 12-month position with a full range of health and retirement benefits. Salary will be commensurate with experience.

Company Description

It all started when engineer Fred Luddy wrote code that automated a tedious task for his coworker, Phyllis. She cried tears of joy. That moment inspired Fred to build a company that could do that for everyone—freeing people from busywork so they could focus on meaningful work. Today, ServiceNow is the AI control tower for business reinvention. Our ServiceNow AI platform brings together any AI, any data, and any workflow— helping 85% of the Fortune 500® work smarter, faster, and better. We're building an AI-native culture where technology and talent are unstoppable together. And we're just getting started.

Join us to put AI to work for people.

Job Description

l

Role overview

The Global Director, Global Technology Partnerships leads the Partner Technology Architect (PTA) team across ServiceNow’s technology ecosystem; hyperscalers, ISVs, and strategic technology partnerships spanning every geography. As the persistent partner-facing technical authority within the Partner Technology Acceleration Group (PTAG), this leader turns platform and AI depth into co-innovation at scale across ServiceNow’s technology routes to market.

The role carries three accountabilities: accelerate adoption of ServiceNow’s full platform and AI portfolio through the technology-partner ecosystem; grow the paths to revenue that flow through the ServiceNow Store, co-sell, and partner-influenced motions; and build the architectural credibility that positions ServiceNow as the workflow engine of the enterprise AI market. It pairs deep technical leadership with business development accountability, architectural authority, and commercial impact in one seat.

Why this role matters

Technology partnerships sit at the highest-leverage, most complex edge of the ecosystem. Hyperscalers are partners and platforms at once, ISVs monetize their own intellectual property on top of ServiceNow, and frontier-AI and advisory partners move faster than any single motion can keep pace with. This leader sets the technical strategy that turns those relationships into repeatable, co-innovated solutions and gives the field a credible architecture to sell with. Without that technical authority, even the strongest partnerships produce integrations that never scale into revenue.

Key responsibilities

Ecosystem strategy and orchestration

Define and drive the technical strategy for ServiceNow’s technology-partner ecosystem across hyperscaler, ISV, and strategic technology partnerships, so cross-partner patterns compound into ecosystem-wide momentum.
Own the partner prioritization model weighing technical readiness, co-innovation intent, and customer pipeline alignment to focus PTA coverage where ServiceNow wins and grows.
Translate PTAG and GPC strategy into ecosystem execution across every geography.
Build repeatable, scalable enablement that extends the team’s reach beyond its own capacity—creating a reusable content payload for recruiting and onboarding ISV partners and for positioning hyperscaler as a route to market, then activating it through GEO SC leadership so field teams and partners can lead these opportunities independently rather than depending on the team for every engagement.

Technical authority and co-innovation

Lead the PTA team as the persistent technical authority for the ecosystem; technical discovery, architectural validation, and competitive positioning that accelerate partner-led opportunities.
Drive AI-first co-innovation with partners, applying ServiceNow reference architectures and design standards to shape joint solutions and repeatable offerings.
Accelerate partner-built solutions through the ServiceNow Store surfacing co-innovation opportunities, guiding certification-ready design, and coordinating go-to-market with partners.
Grow partner mindshare, consumption, and solution quality by evangelizing ServiceNow platform and AI capabilities across the partner community.

Executive partnership management

Serve as the named ServiceNow technical counterpart to VP- and SVP-level leadership at each strategic technology partner.
Represent ServiceNow’s platform and AI strategy at partner executive forums, joint steering committees, and industry events.
Build trusted-advisor relationships with partner C-suite (CTO, CAIO, CDO) to shape practice investment and platform adoption roadmaps.
Navigate coexist-and-compete dynamics where a partner may be collaborator, platform, and customer at once.

Team leadership and talent

Build, inspire, and develop the global PTA team, establishing clear career paths, succession plans, and talent pipelines to support ecosystem growth.
Establish the operating model; engagement cadences, reporting rhythms, and knowledge-sharing practices that keep a distributed team aligned.
Drive recruiting for senior partner-facing technical talent, sourcing from platform companies, hyperscalers, and advanced consultancies.
Foster a PTA community of practice that turns cross-partner learning into collective technical strength.

Qualifications

15+ years in technology leadership spanning pre-sales, solution consulting, solution architecture, or technical partnership management at enterprise scale, with demonstrated success in partner-ecosystem contexts.
10+ years of second-line leadership building and scaling front-line technical teams across diverse geographies, with strong coaching and talent development.
Deep technical credibility across enterprise platforms, cloud architectures, and the AI stack—foundation models, agentic architectures, AI governance, and enterprise AI adoption patterns—with the ability to translate capability into business value.
Fluency in technology-partner go-to-market: hyperscaler co-sell, ISV and marketplace economics, and strategic technology alliances, including their business models and co-innovation requirements.
Proven track record growing partner-sourced and partner-influenced revenue through measurable pipeline growth, deal velocity, and win-rate impact.
Executive presence to engage C-level partner stakeholders, present to large audiences, and build strategic relationships across organizational boundaries.
Experience leading distributed, high-autonomy technical teams across multiple geographies.

Preferred Qualifications

ServiceNow platform and AI portfolio experience, or deep familiarity with enterprise SaaS platforms and workflow automation.
Experience building or scaling partner marketplace or Store programs at a major technology platform.
Hyperscaler co-sell experience across public cloud marketplaces (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud).
Co-innovation framework or design-thinking expertise.
Background in developer relations, partner engineering, or technology alliance program management.

Location and travel

Global, with approximately 40–50% travel across partner sites, ServiceNow offices, and joint customer engagements.

jobs.description:
Artivion Overview

Headquartered in suburban Atlanta, Georgia, Artivion, Inc. is a medical device company focused on developing simple, elegant solutions that address cardiac and vascular surgeons’ most difficult challenges in treating patients with aortic diseases. Artivion’s four major groups of products include: aortic stent grafts, surgical sealants, On-X mechanical heart valves, and implantable cardiac and vascular human tissues. Artivion has over 1,600 employees worldwide with sales representation in over 100 countries. The Company has manufacturing facilities located in Atlanta, Georgia, Austin, Texas and Hechingen, Germany. Additionally, it has sales and distribution offices in various countries throughout Europe, Asia, and South America. For additional information about Artivion, visit our website, www.artivion.com.

Position Overview

We are seeking a Director of Infrastructure Operations & Strategy to provide strategic, operational, financial, and people leadership for enterprise infrastructure operations, engineering, and platform services across servers, storage platforms, cloud connectivity, data center services, monitoring, service restoration, and related resilience capabilities. Cybersecurity remains an enabling discipline, with the Director accountable for ensuring appropriate controls are embedded into infrastructure architecture, operations, lifecycle management, and recovery practices.

This role owns the infrastructure operations model, infrastructure roadmap, service reliability objectives, capacity and lifecycle planning, operational support processes, vendor and partner performance, and financial stewardship for the infrastructure portfolio. The Director supports the annual budgeting, forecasting, capital and operating expense planning process, budget variance management, and cost optimization while ensuring infrastructure operations and investments align with business priorities, risk tolerance, and enterprise technology strategy.

The successful candidate is expected to lead through managers, engineers, operations teams, and cross-functional partners while remaining sufficiently technical to guide architecture decisions, direct high-severity incident response, and support executive-level communication during critical events. The role balances strategic planning, operational execution, financial discipline, governance, and measurable improvement in service availability, resiliency, performance, scalability, and security posture.

Responsibilities

Enterprise Infrastructure Strategy, Engineering & Operations Leadership

Set the multi-year strategy, standards, and operating model for enterprise infrastructure operations and engineering across compute, storage, cloud, data center, and core platform services.
Lead the design, implementation, operation, and modernization of infrastructure services to meet availability, performance, scalability, recoverability, security, and supportability requirements.
Establish governance for architecture decisions, technical standards, lifecycle management, service ownership, operational readiness, change readiness, and production support.
Prioritize infrastructure operations and engineering initiatives based on business value, service reliability, risk reduction, regulatory needs, technical debt, and total cost of ownership.

Infrastructure Operations & Service Management

Own day-to-day infrastructure operations, including monitoring, incident response, change execution, service restoration, operational handoffs, and escalation management.

Resilience, Disaster Recovery & Cyber Recovery

People Leadership, Governance & Stakeholder Engagement

Lead, coach, and develop infrastructure engineering and operations teams; establish goals, performance expectations, succession plans, and talent development plans.
Develop clear operating rhythms for service reviews, operations reviews, project governance, financial reviews, incident reviews, problem reviews, and executive reporting.

12-18 years of progressive experience in infrastructure engineering, infrastructure operations, enterprise platforms, cloud, working knowledge of networking concepts related to systems, data center operations, or related technology leadership roles.

Demonstrated experience owning departmental or portfolio-level budgets, including capital and operating expense planning, forecasting, budget variance management, vendor spend, managed service costs, and cost optimization.

Technical & Operational Leadership

Strong experience with high availability, fault-tolerant design, performance optimization, capacity planning, disaster recovery architecture, and RTO/RPO ownership.

Governance, Financial & Vendor Management

jobs.title: Vice President of Technology
jobs.description:
Location:
Auburn, WA (onsite/hybrid)
Reports to:
Jon Bach, Founder & President
Team:
2 IT technicians, 1 software developer, 1 TPM, plans to add 1-2 senior developers

About Puget Systems

Puget Systems builds high-performance custom workstations and servers for professionals in content creation, engineering, scientific computing, and AI/ML. For over two decades we've differentiated ourselves through obsessive quality, published reliability data, in-house benchmarking research (Puget Labs), and a consultative approach to every sale. We're a ~75-person company that competes with billion-dollar OEMs by being smarter, faster, and more genuinely customer-focused than they can be.

A significant part of that advantage is invisible to customers: a custom-built internal business operating system that runs configuration, quoting, purchasing, inventory, and production across the company. It was built by our founder over many years, and it is deeply fitted to how we work. It is a strategic advantage, but requires a full technology team to maintain and build on top of it.

About the Role

Until a few years ago, software and IT at Puget Systems were run personally by our founder. The technology department that exists today is young: a small, capable team of four people, informal processes, and a homegrown platform that is accompanied by a lot of tribal knowledge. We are looking for a VP of Technology to take true ownership of the systems, the team, and the roadmap and mature it into a sustainable system without losing the pragmatism and specialization that made it valuable in the first place.

This will always be a small team. If you're looking to build a large organization, this is not the role for you. But if you want to be the most senior technical person at a successful, profitable, and respected company, leading a small but effective team with outsized strategic impact, and a seat on the Executive Leadership Team… read on!

What You'll Own

The internal business platform.
Take over stewardship of our custom-built business OS from the founder. Learn the extensive legacy code base deeply, and lead the strategy for what to maintain, refactor, replace, or retire with deliberate architecture decisions rather than a reflex to rewrite. The platform is built on the LAMP stack.
The software team and products.
Mentor our software developers into confident, capable engineers, and hire 1-2 senior developers to raise the technical ceiling. Establish and maintain standards for the software team: source control discipline, code review, release management, testing, and build a culture of ownership and delivery of results.
The IT team and infrastructure.
Manage the internal IT team and oversee IT operations for the whole company. Oversee network configuration for reliability and security, and maintain our internal servers and infrastructure across onsite, colocation, and cloud environments. Craft our plan for 24/7 incident response, and follow it.
The public website.
Own www.pugetsystems.com, our WordPress-based front-end site that is our storefront and the home of our published research. This includes the API integrations that tie it back to our internal systems.
The internal website.
Codenamed “NAV” , this is the internal business OS that has an extensive code base and history. It will be a significant effort to learn this system and maintain it. Everyone who has come before you has under-estimated this system.
Data integrations and reporting.
Manage our connections to external platforms and services. We have decided that “NAV” is the central data hub. You will own this data, and its connectors to BI reporting, ensuring the business has reliable, trustworthy data to run on.
Cybersecurity.
Maintain and enforce cybersecurity standards company-wide, including the specific requirements embedded in our customer contracts. Own backup and disaster recovery.
Documentation and process maturity.
Establish the practices a mature technology organization needs, including documentation, well-defined processes, and task management workflows in ClickUp. We want this to be sized appropriately for a 75-person company, not over-complicated. Build internal support and prioritization processes so the rest of the company knows how to work with the team.
Budget and financial management.
Execute the annual budgeting process for the department, report expenses via Ramp, and manage the team to its monthly budget.
A seat on the Executive Leadership Team.
This role sits on the ELT, the group responsible for shaping the strategy and direction of the company. You'll represent technology at that table and you'll be expected to contribute to long term company-level decisions well beyond your own department.
Technology strategy.
Partner with the founder and leadership team to decide where technology investment creates competitive advantage, and where it doesn't. Translate business needs into a realistic roadmap, and deliver on it.

Where This Role Grows: Puget Labs

Puget Labs is the heart and soul of Puget Systems, and the moat around our business. It consists of two teams working as two sides of the same coin:

The Performance Lab
studies real end-user workflows and benchmarks computer hardware against them. They publish widely-read articles and are recognized figureheads in the industry. Puget Systems has built its reputation on this work.
The R&D Lab
engages directly with the PC hardware ecosystem (component manufacturers and vendors) to qualify components and design the laptops, workstations, servers, and storage that meet the workflow needs the Performance Lab identifies.

This VP will not own Puget Labs on day one. The job starts with software and IT. But once that foundation is well in hand, leadership of Puget Labs is the intended growth path for this role, bringing the company's core differentiator under the same technology leadership. Candidates should be genuinely excited by that trajectory: this is ultimately a role that grows into stewarding what makes Puget Systems special.

Who You Are

A player-coach, permanently.
You are a strong hands-on engineer who still writes and reviews code, and you expect to keep doing so.
Experienced with inherited systems.
You've taken ownership of large, long-lived, lightly-documented codebases before (ideally from the original author) and you know how to handle that transition.
A builder of teams.
You have a track record of growing junior developers into strong ones, and of hiring well. You mentor others, even those not on your team.
Pragmatic about processes.
You know that process and documentation sets up a team for success, and you calibrate to company size.
Broad across software and IT.
You're credible leading both application development and IT/infrastructure/security for a mid-sized business.
A clear communicator with non-technical leaders.
You can explain tradeoffs, set expectations, and earn trust across sales, production, and operations teams whose daily work runs on your systems.
Financially accountable.
You've owned a department budget before and treat it as a real commitment, including planning annually, tracking monthly, and making tradeoffs transparently.

Qualifications

10+ years in software development and/or IT, including 3+ years leading a technology function as Director, VP, CTO, or Head of Engineering/IT.
Direct experience owning both software and IT for a mid-sized business (roughly 50–500 employees). We're looking for proof you've done this specific job, not a scaled-down version of a big-company role, and not a first step up from team lead.
A track record of maturing a technology organization: you can point to specific practices you established, systems you stabilized or replaced, and people who grew under your leadership.
Deep hands-on proficiency with the LAMP stack, which our internal platform is built on, plus working fluency with a modern JavaScript framework (we've tentatively standardized on Vue for new projects); WordPress and API-driven integration experience is a plus.
Prior ownership of a department budget.

Physical Requirements

Prolonged periods sitting at a desk and working on a computer.
Able to work from home or office.
Able to travel for trade shows and other activities.

Nice to Have

Experience in manufacturing, e-commerce, or configure-to-order businesses
Experience working directly with a founder/owner in a succession or transition capacity
Familiarity with ERP internal systems, whether homegrown or commercial
Experience building or managing data lakes, data pipelines, and BI reporting stacks
Experience meeting security requirements (e.g., customer security requirements, SOC2, NIST, or CMMC frameworks)

Why This Role Is Worth It

You'll inherit a genuinely interesting technical asset, a supportive founder who wants to hand it off well, a profitable and stable company with a strong reputation, and a team eager to grow. Your decisions will affect the entire company, and the role grows into stewardship of Puget Labs, who is the industry-respected source of our reputation. Few VP roles offer this much ownership with this little bureaucracy.

PTO and STO - Standard policy is 2 weeks PTO to start, +1 day / year until 4 week maximum
Paid holidays - 8 days + 2 floating holiday per year
Paid parental leave - 3 weeks
Paid Medical Hardship Leave - up to 2 weeks / year
Paid jury duty leave - up to 2 weeks / year
4% match on 401(k), immediate vesting
Volunteer Matching Program
Wellness Reimbursement Program
Company-sponsored financial counseling

Applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment visa.

jobs.title: Vice President of Engineering
jobs.description:
Hybrid/In Person: Boston, MA Headquarters (2-4 days/week)

LineVision is hiring an operating executive who can turn grid intelligence software and hardware into the systems regulated utilities depend on to run their operations.

We are seeking a VP of Engineering
to own engineering delivery across our software and hardware organizations. You will run delivery of Nexus Core, our next-generation multi-tenant SaaS platform for dynamic line rating, as it moves past launch and into daily operations for a growing base of utility customers. You will also bring the engineering judgment behind the current wave of hardware evolution on our field-deployed sensor. If you want to build and run a development organization at pace across software and hardware, and be accountable for the commitments regulated utilities depend on, join us at LineVision
, Built In Boston Best Places to Work !

What will you do?

Core Responsibilities And Key Performance Objectives

Lead engineering delivery across Platform, Applications, Embedded Software, Data Science, and Hardware Engineering, with every director and manager in these functions reporting through this role.
Drive Nexus Core's ongoing release cadence, across multi-tenant SaaS and on-premise deployments for regulated, international customers.
Guide the field-deployed sensor fleet, including health monitoring, lifecycle management, and the next-generation sensor launch, bringing hardware design judgment to component and subsystem trade-offs.
Establish delivery standards and a reporting cadence across the org: milestone-level, on track or not, with a named owner for every commitment.
Represent engineering to the executive team and partner with Product, Sales, Customer Success, and Finance on delivery commitments, forecasting, and customer escalations.

Within the first 3 months:

Develop a working command of Nexus Core's architecture and release history, the sensor fleet's current state, and the org structure across all four functions.
Stand up a milestone-level reporting cadence with named owners across Platform, Applications, Data Science, and Hardware/Firmware.
Build working relationships with Product, Sales, Customer Success, and Finance leaders on delivery commitments and forecasting.

Within the first 6 months:

Run Nexus Core's release cadence against hard external commitments for existing SaaS and on-premise customers.
Drive the component and subsystem decisions for the next-generation sensor launch, working closely with the hardware/firmware manager.
Next-generation sensor design decisions are locked and moving through execution toward launch

Milestones within the first year:

Nexus Core is on a predictable release cadence that consistently meets external commitments across SaaS and on-premise deployments.
The org is staffed with strong managers and senior ICs across Platform, Applications, Data Science, and Hardware/Firmware.

How To Succeed In This Role

Key Competencies

Critical Thinking: Diagnose complex delivery, architecture, and hardware trade-offs across software and hardware. Push the organization toward evidence-based decisions over assumptions.
Taking Ownership: Own delivery outcomes for Nexus Core and the sensor fleet end to end. Hold every commitment to a named owner and a clear status.
Judgment & Decision Making: Weigh risk and opportunity across competing priorities in software and hardware delivery. Make the call, communicate it clearly, and stand behind it.
Stakeholder Management: Align Product, Sales, Customer Success, and Finance on delivery commitments and forecasts. Represent engineering credibly to the executive team.

Essential Skills

12+ years in engineering, with several years leading engineering organizations that shipped production software to external customers, preferably in industrial markets.
Track record delivering a multi-tenant SaaS platform from architecture through general availability, then running its ongoing release cadence against hard external commitments.
Experience running on-premise or privately deployed software for enterprise customers with strict security or compliance requirements.
Hands-on hardware design experience for industrial or field-deployed products, including environmental hardening and certifications (UL, CE, FCC, IP-rated enclosures).

What Sets The Best Candidates Apart

Startup experience ramping a company from 1-N.
NERC CIP or comparable regulated critical-infrastructure experience.
Personally built data products or analytics platforms, not just partnered with the team building them.
Grid intelligence or dynamic line rating domain experience, or direct hardware/firmware, embedded, or OTA background.

Reporting & Team Structure

Reports to the CTO.
Lead an organization of 35+ full-time leaders, engineers and contractors, spanning Platform, Applications, and Embedded Software, Data Science, and Hardware Engineering.
Collaborates closely with Product, Sales, Customer Success, and Finance.

What does joining LineVision mean for you?

Impact. Your talent, time, and energy will critically impact our success in delivering utilities with grid intelligence to enable affordable, reliable power.
Ownership. You will hold broad responsibilities with high autonomy and trust in a communicative, collaborative, and fast-paced environment.
Flexibility. You will be empowered to maintain work-life balance with trust-based PTO.
Real World Innovation. You will lead a motivated, high-performing team working with cutting edge, patented technology to help utilities meet the demands of an AI-powered future.

Who We Are…

LineVision is a grid-enhancing technology company enabling electric utilities to deliver affordable, reliable power and accelerate the electrification of the global economy. Our grid intelligence platform delivers the most accurate, network-wide dynamic line ratings and enables safer, more reliable grid operations with a combination of optical sensors and advanced environmental modeling. LineVision's global customer base includes eight of the ten largest US utilities, including National Grid, Southern Company, and Exelon.

We are LineVisionaries:
We are Innovators: We light the way with tenacious creativity and do good work.
We are Empowered: With high trust and high autonomy, the floor is yours, and the opportunity is ours.
We are Welcoming: Come as you are, our doors are open. We are better together.
We are Trusted Partners: We elevate our customer champions through shared thought leadership. We deliver on commitments.
We are All In: We are building a community of passionate individuals who want to dent the universe.

At LineVision there's no such thing as a "perfect" candidate. We are looking for exceptional people who want to make a positive impact through their work and facilitate an organization where everyone can thrive. So whatever background you bring with you, please apply if this role would make you excited to come to work every day.
Meet our team, and understand our mission: https://www.linevisioninc.com/about-us
