new_jobs.title: DIRECTOR OF RESEARCH TECHNOLOGY SERVICES
new_jobs.description:
DIRECTOR OF RESEARCH TECHNOLOGY SERVICES

JOB SUMMARY
Under the general direction of the Chief Information Officer, provides executive, technical, and operational leadership for technology services supporting the University’s research enterprise within Information Technology Services (ITS). The Director is responsible for developing and implementing solutions, policies, and services that advance the University’s research mission through effective use of technology. The Director serves as the primary liaison between ITS, the Office of the Vice President for Research (OVPR), faculty researchers, research centers, and other stakeholders to ensure that technology services effectively support current and emerging research needs and has a dotted line reporting relationship to the Vice President for Research, Innovation and Entrepreneurship.
The Director provides leadership for research computing services, secure research environments, research data services, research cybersecurity initiatives, compliance-driven research technologies, artificial intelligence and emerging research technologies, and strategic research technology planning. The Director works collaboratively with all ITS teams to coordinate the delivery of research technology services across the University. The Director also works with peers at UConn Health’s to help meet the needs of researchers across UConn and UConn Health through a shared information technology resources model.
For activities related to these responsibilities, the Director interacts and coordinates with University administration, OVPR leadership, faculty researchers, campus and department technology leaders, research centers and institutes, technology advisory groups, external partners, and individual members of the University community across UConn and UConn Health. The Director serves as an advisor to the CIO and other University leaders on research technology, governance, and secure service delivery. The Director coordinates and participates in high-level technology assessments, program planning, and serves as a member of the ITS Leadership Team.
The Director maintains budgets and staffing levels appropriate to assigned responsibilities, oversees personnel planning, hiring, and assessment, attends conferences and professional development activities, and interacts with external peers to maintain knowledge of current issues, opportunities, and best practices in research technology services.
DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
• Provides leadership and direction to the University on research technology services, research computing, secure research environments, research data management, research cybersecurity, and emerging technologies supporting the University’s research mission and priorities
• Develops and maintains a long-term strategic vision and roadmap for research technology services in partnership with University leadership, OVPR, faculty researchers, and ITS leadership.
• Serves as the primary relationship manager between ITS and the research community, ensuring that researcher needs, priorities, and challenges are understood and addressed through effective technology solutions and services.
• Establishes and maintains strong partnerships with faculty, research centers, OVPR leadership, and external stakeholders to identify opportunities, improve service delivery, and advance research initiatives.
• Oversees the portfolio of research technology initiatives and projects, ensuring effective planning, communication, risk management, prioritization, resource coordination, and successful service delivery.
• Provides technical leadership and coordination for secure research computing initiatives supporting regulated research activities, including environments requiring compliance with NIST 800-171, CMMC, HIPAA, and other applicable regulatory frameworks.
• Works collaboratively with ITS infrastructure, security, networking, enterprise systems, cloud services, and application teams to ensure research technology services are aligned with University standards, policies, and strategic objectives.
• Provides technical leadership and coordination for research computing resources, cloud-based research environments, research data services, and advanced computing capabilities .
• Identifies opportunities to leverage emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence, advanced analytics, cloud computing, and research data platforms, to support the University's research enterprise.
• Oversees staffing, hiring, training, mentoring, performance evaluation, and discipline for assigned employees and serves as the departmental representative for all union-related issues.
• Develops and maintains budgets associated with research technology services and provides guidance regarding technology investments, contracts, software licensing, cloud services, and vendor relationships.
• Establishes service metrics and performance measures to evaluate effectiveness, improve service quality, and ensure alignment with institutional goals and researcher needs.
• Prepares periodic reports regarding strategic initiatives, project portfolios, operational activities, budgets, service performance, and emerging opportunities.
• Interacts with ITS senior leadership, University governance groups, technology planning committees, and IT leaders across th UConn and UConn Health to ensure coordination and alignment of research technology initiatives.
• Performs other duties as required.
MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS
• Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution.
• Minimum of ten (10) years of progressively responsible experience in information technology, research computing, research technology services, or a related field.
• Minimum of five (5) years of higher education experience in a research-intensive university or comparable research environment.
• Experience supporting technology services for faculty researchers and research programs.
• Experience with research computing, secure research environments, research data services, cloud technologies, or related research technology disciplines.
• Experience working with compliance requirements related to research, including NIST 800-171, CMMC, HIPAA, FERPA, or other applicable frameworks.
• Excellent and demonstrated project and portfolio management skills, including strategic planning, prioritization, resource coordination, budget management, and successful delivery of complex initiatives.
• Strong personnel supervision skills, including employee performance management, mentoring, communication, team development, and organizational leadership.
• Demonstrated ability to build partnerships and maintain productive relationships with faculty, researchers, administrators, and technology professionals.
• Demonstrated ability to act decisively and solve problems through creative, collaborative, and strategic thinking.
• Ability to identify key issues in complex situations, evaluate alternatives, and develop effective strategies for resolution.
• Ability to translate strategic objectives into operational plans and align resources with institutional priorities.
• Proven leadership, communication, and relationship-building skills with diverse university constituencies.
• Ability to build effective teams that emphasize service, partnership, collaboration, accountability, and continuous improvement.
PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS
• Advanced degree from an accredited institution.
• Experience in a leadership role supporting research technology services within a major research university.
• Experience collaborating with offices supporting research administration, compliance, sponsored programs, or research security.
• Relevant certifications related to project management, information security, cloud technologies, research administration, or technology leadership.
• Experience developing technology governance structures and stakeholder engagement programs.
APPOINTMENT TERMS
This is a full-time, 12-month position with a full range of health and retirement benefits. Salary will be commensurate with experience.

Company Description

It all started when engineer Fred Luddy wrote code that automated a tedious task for his coworker, Phyllis. She cried tears of joy. That moment inspired Fred to build a company that could do that for everyone—freeing people from busywork so they could focus on meaningful work. Today, ServiceNow is the AI control tower for business reinvention. Our ServiceNow AI platform brings together any AI, any data, and any workflow— helping 85% of the Fortune 500® work smarter, faster, and better. We're building an AI-native culture where technology and talent are unstoppable together. And we're just getting started.

Join us to put AI to work for people.

Job Description

l

Role overview

The Global Director, Global Technology Partnerships leads the Partner Technology Architect (PTA) team across ServiceNow’s technology ecosystem; hyperscalers, ISVs, and strategic technology partnerships spanning every geography. As the persistent partner-facing technical authority within the Partner Technology Acceleration Group (PTAG), this leader turns platform and AI depth into co-innovation at scale across ServiceNow’s technology routes to market.

The role carries three accountabilities: accelerate adoption of ServiceNow’s full platform and AI portfolio through the technology-partner ecosystem; grow the paths to revenue that flow through the ServiceNow Store, co-sell, and partner-influenced motions; and build the architectural credibility that positions ServiceNow as the workflow engine of the enterprise AI market. It pairs deep technical leadership with business development accountability, architectural authority, and commercial impact in one seat.

Why this role matters

Technology partnerships sit at the highest-leverage, most complex edge of the ecosystem. Hyperscalers are partners and platforms at once, ISVs monetize their own intellectual property on top of ServiceNow, and frontier-AI and advisory partners move faster than any single motion can keep pace with. This leader sets the technical strategy that turns those relationships into repeatable, co-innovated solutions and gives the field a credible architecture to sell with. Without that technical authority, even the strongest partnerships produce integrations that never scale into revenue.

Key responsibilities

Ecosystem strategy and orchestration

Define and drive the technical strategy for ServiceNow’s technology-partner ecosystem across hyperscaler, ISV, and strategic technology partnerships, so cross-partner patterns compound into ecosystem-wide momentum.
Own the partner prioritization model weighing technical readiness, co-innovation intent, and customer pipeline alignment to focus PTA coverage where ServiceNow wins and grows.
Translate PTAG and GPC strategy into ecosystem execution across every geography.
Build repeatable, scalable enablement that extends the team’s reach beyond its own capacity—creating a reusable content payload for recruiting and onboarding ISV partners and for positioning hyperscaler as a route to market, then activating it through GEO SC leadership so field teams and partners can lead these opportunities independently rather than depending on the team for every engagement.

Technical authority and co-innovation

Lead the PTA team as the persistent technical authority for the ecosystem; technical discovery, architectural validation, and competitive positioning that accelerate partner-led opportunities.
Drive AI-first co-innovation with partners, applying ServiceNow reference architectures and design standards to shape joint solutions and repeatable offerings.
Accelerate partner-built solutions through the ServiceNow Store surfacing co-innovation opportunities, guiding certification-ready design, and coordinating go-to-market with partners.
Grow partner mindshare, consumption, and solution quality by evangelizing ServiceNow platform and AI capabilities across the partner community.

Executive partnership management

Serve as the named ServiceNow technical counterpart to VP- and SVP-level leadership at each strategic technology partner.
Represent ServiceNow’s platform and AI strategy at partner executive forums, joint steering committees, and industry events.
Build trusted-advisor relationships with partner C-suite (CTO, CAIO, CDO) to shape practice investment and platform adoption roadmaps.
Navigate coexist-and-compete dynamics where a partner may be collaborator, platform, and customer at once.

Team leadership and talent

Build, inspire, and develop the global PTA team, establishing clear career paths, succession plans, and talent pipelines to support ecosystem growth.
Establish the operating model; engagement cadences, reporting rhythms, and knowledge-sharing practices that keep a distributed team aligned.
Drive recruiting for senior partner-facing technical talent, sourcing from platform companies, hyperscalers, and advanced consultancies.
Foster a PTA community of practice that turns cross-partner learning into collective technical strength.

Qualifications

15+ years in technology leadership spanning pre-sales, solution consulting, solution architecture, or technical partnership management at enterprise scale, with demonstrated success in partner-ecosystem contexts.
10+ years of second-line leadership building and scaling front-line technical teams across diverse geographies, with strong coaching and talent development.
Deep technical credibility across enterprise platforms, cloud architectures, and the AI stack—foundation models, agentic architectures, AI governance, and enterprise AI adoption patterns—with the ability to translate capability into business value.
Fluency in technology-partner go-to-market: hyperscaler co-sell, ISV and marketplace economics, and strategic technology alliances, including their business models and co-innovation requirements.
Proven track record growing partner-sourced and partner-influenced revenue through measurable pipeline growth, deal velocity, and win-rate impact.
Executive presence to engage C-level partner stakeholders, present to large audiences, and build strategic relationships across organizational boundaries.
Experience leading distributed, high-autonomy technical teams across multiple geographies.

Preferred Qualifications

ServiceNow platform and AI portfolio experience, or deep familiarity with enterprise SaaS platforms and workflow automation.
Experience building or scaling partner marketplace or Store programs at a major technology platform.
Hyperscaler co-sell experience across public cloud marketplaces (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud).
Co-innovation framework or design-thinking expertise.
Background in developer relations, partner engineering, or technology alliance program management.

Location and travel

Global, with approximately 40–50% travel across partner sites, ServiceNow offices, and joint customer engagements.

, plus equity (when applicable), variable/incentive compensation and benefits. Sales positions generally offer a competitive On Target Earnings (OTE) incentive compensation structure. new_jobs.description:
Artivion Overview

Headquartered in suburban Atlanta, Georgia, Artivion, Inc. is a medical device company focused on developing simple, elegant solutions that address cardiac and vascular surgeons’ most difficult challenges in treating patients with aortic diseases. Artivion’s four major groups of products include: aortic stent grafts, surgical sealants, On-X mechanical heart valves, and implantable cardiac and vascular human tissues. Artivion has over 1,600 employees worldwide with sales representation in over 100 countries. The Company has manufacturing facilities located in Atlanta, Georgia, Austin, Texas and Hechingen, Germany. Additionally, it has sales and distribution offices in various countries throughout Europe, Asia, and South America. For additional information about Artivion, visit our website, www.artivion.com.

Position Overview

We are seeking a Director of Infrastructure Operations & Strategy to provide strategic, operational, financial, and people leadership for enterprise infrastructure operations, engineering, and platform services across servers, storage platforms, cloud connectivity, data center services, monitoring, service restoration, and related resilience capabilities. Cybersecurity remains an enabling discipline, with the Director accountable for ensuring appropriate controls are embedded into infrastructure architecture, operations, lifecycle management, and recovery practices.

This role owns the infrastructure operations model, infrastructure roadmap, service reliability objectives, capacity and lifecycle planning, operational support processes, vendor and partner performance, and financial stewardship for the infrastructure portfolio. The Director supports the annual budgeting, forecasting, capital and operating expense planning process, budget variance management, and cost optimization while ensuring infrastructure operations and investments align with business priorities, risk tolerance, and enterprise technology strategy.

The successful candidate is expected to lead through managers, engineers, operations teams, and cross-functional partners while remaining sufficiently technical to guide architecture decisions, direct high-severity incident response, and support executive-level communication during critical events. The role balances strategic planning, operational execution, financial discipline, governance, and measurable improvement in service availability, resiliency, performance, scalability, and security posture.

Responsibilities

Enterprise Infrastructure Strategy, Engineering & Operations Leadership

Set the multi-year strategy, standards, and operating model for enterprise infrastructure operations and engineering across compute, storage, cloud, data center, and core platform services.
Lead the design, implementation, operation, and modernization of infrastructure services to meet availability, performance, scalability, recoverability, security, and supportability requirements.
Establish governance for architecture decisions, technical standards, lifecycle management, service ownership, operational readiness, change readiness, and production support.
Prioritize infrastructure operations and engineering initiatives based on business value, service reliability, risk reduction, regulatory needs, technical debt, and total cost of ownership.

Infrastructure Operations & Service Management

Own day-to-day infrastructure operations, including monitoring, incident response, change execution, service restoration, operational handoffs, and escalation management.
Establish and manage operating metrics for infrastructure services, including availability, performance, capacity, incident trends, change success rates, aging problems, and service-level performance.
Drive operational discipline through standard operating procedures, runbooks, knowledge management, event management, post-incident reviews, and continuous service improvement.
Ensure infrastructure operations are aligned with ITSM practices and integrated with service desk, application, cybersecurity, enterprise architecture, and business continuity processes.
Lead infrastructure operational readiness for new systems, acquisitions, integrations, site changes, manufacturing/plant requirements, and major business or technology initiatives.

Financial Management, Budgeting & Cost Optimization

Assist with infrastructure financial planning, including annual operating and capital budgets, multi-year investment planning, forecasting, and budget variance management.
Manage vendor spend, licensing, maintenance contracts, cloud consumption, hardware refresh cycles, managed services, and infrastructure project financials.
Partner with Finance, Procurement, Network, IT leadership, and business stakeholders to build business cases, track ROI, manage accruals, and support funding decisions.
Identify and execute cost optimization opportunities while preserving resilience, compliance, performance, and service quality.

Server, Compute & Platform Management

Oversee architecture, build, configuration, patching, performance, capacity planning, operations, and lifecycle management of physical, virtual, and cloud compute environments.
Ensure reliability and operational excellence across Windows, Linux, virtualization, and cloud compute platforms.
Drive standardization, automation, observability, and configuration management across compute environments.

Storage, Backup & Data Platform Leadership

Lead architecture and operations of enterprise storage platforms, including SAN, NAS, object, backup, replication, immutable storage, and cloud storage services.
Ensure data durability, recoverability, performance, encryption, retention alignment, and lifecycle management for critical enterprise data.
Define storage tiering, protection, replication, and recovery strategies aligned with business criticality, operational needs, and cost objectives.

Resilience, Disaster Recovery & Cyber Recovery

Assist and guide infrastructure disaster recovery, cyber recovery, and business continuity capabilities from a platform, operations, and service-readiness perspective.
Ensure systems are recoverable within defined RTO/RPO targets and that recovery capabilities are tested, documented, operationalized, and continuously improved.
Lead recovery planning and executive communication during high-severity outages, cyber events, operational disruptions, or resilience exercises.

People Leadership, Governance & Stakeholder Engagement

Lead, coach, and develop infrastructure engineering and operations teams; establish goals, performance expectations, succession plans, and talent development plans.
Develop clear operating rhythms for service reviews, operations reviews, project governance, financial reviews, incident reviews, problem reviews, and executive reporting.
Serve as a liaison between infrastructure operations, infrastructure engineering, cybersecurity, IT leadership, Finance, Procurement, business leaders, and external partners.
Communicate infrastructure service health, operational risks, financial outlook, project status, and investment priorities to executive leadership.

Qualifications

Education & Experience

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, Business, or related field; Master's degree preferred.
12-18 years of progressive experience in infrastructure engineering, infrastructure operations, enterprise platforms, cloud, working knowledge of networking concepts related to systems, data center operations, or related technology leadership roles.
Minimum 5-8 years of people leadership experience, including leadership of managers, senior engineers, operations teams, distributed teams, or vendor/managed service teams.
Demonstrated experience owning departmental or portfolio-level budgets, including capital and operating expense planning, forecasting, budget variance management, vendor spend, managed service costs, and cost optimization.

Technical & Operational Leadership

Proven track record building, scaling, modernizing, and operating infrastructure platforms and operations functions across on-premises, hybrid cloud, and cloud-connected environments.
Strong working knowledge of server platforms, virtualization, cloud compute, storage systems, backup/recovery, replication, routing, switching, firewalls, segmentation, SD-WAN, monitoring, observability, and core infrastructure services.
Demonstrated experience leading infrastructure operations, including incident management, problem management, change coordination, service restoration, operational readiness, runbook development, and continuous service improvement.
Ability to operate at the strategic, architectural, operational, and executive communication levels, with enough technical depth to guide decisions during critical incidents.
Strong experience with high availability, fault-tolerant design, performance optimization, capacity planning, disaster recovery architecture, and RTO/RPO ownership.

Governance, Financial & Vendor Management

Experience developing infrastructure roadmaps, lifecycle plans, investment cases, operating metrics, service review forums, governance forums, and executive reporting.
Experience managing vendor relationships, contracts, licensing, renewals, service-level commitments, procurement cycles, managed service performance, and operational escalation paths.
Ability to translate technical risk, service needs, operational gaps, and infrastructure debt into clear financial and business recommendations.

Security, Compliance & Resilience

Working knowledge of cybersecurity principles applied to infrastructure and infrastructure operations, including hardening, patching, identity and access control, segmentation, vulnerability remediation, logging, monitoring, and encryption.
Familiarity with compliance frameworks such as NIST, ISO 27001, HIPAA, SOX, or related control environments as they apply to infrastructure services and operations.
Demonstrated ability to lead high-severity outage, disaster recovery, cyber recovery, or major operational incident response activities, including technical coordination and executive-level communication.

Preferred Credentials

Security certifications such as CISSP, CISM, or related credentials are helpful but not a primary requirement.

new_jobs.title: Vice President of Technology
new_jobs.description:
Location:
Auburn, WA (onsite/hybrid)
Reports to:
Jon Bach, Founder & President
Team:
2 IT technicians, 1 software developer, 1 TPM, plans to add 1-2 senior developers

About Puget Systems

Puget Systems builds high-performance custom workstations and servers for professionals in content creation, engineering, scientific computing, and AI/ML. For over two decades we've differentiated ourselves through obsessive quality, published reliability data, in-house benchmarking research (Puget Labs), and a consultative approach to every sale. We're a ~75-person company that competes with billion-dollar OEMs by being smarter, faster, and more genuinely customer-focused than they can be.

A significant part of that advantage is invisible to customers: a custom-built internal business operating system that runs configuration, quoting, purchasing, inventory, and production across the company. It was built by our founder over many years, and it is deeply fitted to how we work. It is a strategic advantage, but requires a full technology team to maintain and build on top of it.

About the Role

Until a few years ago, software and IT at Puget Systems were run personally by our founder. The technology department that exists today is young: a small, capable team of four people, informal processes, and a homegrown platform that is accompanied by a lot of tribal knowledge. We are looking for a VP of Technology to take true ownership of the systems, the team, and the roadmap and mature it into a sustainable system without losing the pragmatism and specialization that made it valuable in the first place.

This will always be a small team. If you're looking to build a large organization, this is not the role for you. But if you want to be the most senior technical person at a successful, profitable, and respected company, leading a small but effective team with outsized strategic impact, and a seat on the Executive Leadership Team… read on!

What You'll Own

The internal business platform.
Take over stewardship of our custom-built business OS from the founder. Learn the extensive legacy code base deeply, and lead the strategy for what to maintain, refactor, replace, or retire with deliberate architecture decisions rather than a reflex to rewrite. The platform is built on the LAMP stack.
The software team and products.
Mentor our software developers into confident, capable engineers, and hire 1-2 senior developers to raise the technical ceiling. Establish and maintain standards for the software team: source control discipline, code review, release management, testing, and build a culture of ownership and delivery of results.
The IT team and infrastructure.
Manage the internal IT team and oversee IT operations for the whole company. Oversee network configuration for reliability and security, and maintain our internal servers and infrastructure across onsite, colocation, and cloud environments. Craft our plan for 24/7 incident response, and follow it.
The public website.
Own www.pugetsystems.com, our WordPress-based front-end site that is our storefront and the home of our published research. This includes the API integrations that tie it back to our internal systems.
The internal website.
Codenamed “NAV” , this is the internal business OS that has an extensive code base and history. It will be a significant effort to learn this system and maintain it. Everyone who has come before you has under-estimated this system.
Data integrations and reporting.
Manage our connections to external platforms and services. We have decided that “NAV” is the central data hub. You will own this data, and its connectors to BI reporting, ensuring the business has reliable, trustworthy data to run on.
Cybersecurity.
Maintain and enforce cybersecurity standards company-wide, including the specific requirements embedded in our customer contracts. Own backup and disaster recovery.
Documentation and process maturity.
Establish the practices a mature technology organization needs, including documentation, well-defined processes, and task management workflows in ClickUp. We want this to be sized appropriately for a 75-person company, not over-complicated. Build internal support and prioritization processes so the rest of the company knows how to work with the team.
Budget and financial management.
Execute the annual budgeting process for the department, report expenses via Ramp, and manage the team to its monthly budget.
A seat on the Executive Leadership Team.
This role sits on the ELT, the group responsible for shaping the strategy and direction of the company. You'll represent technology at that table and you'll be expected to contribute to long term company-level decisions well beyond your own department.
Technology strategy.
Partner with the founder and leadership team to decide where technology investment creates competitive advantage, and where it doesn't. Translate business needs into a realistic roadmap, and deliver on it.

Where This Role Grows: Puget Labs

Puget Labs is the heart and soul of Puget Systems, and the moat around our business. It consists of two teams working as two sides of the same coin:

The Performance Lab
studies real end-user workflows and benchmarks computer hardware against them. They publish widely-read articles and are recognized figureheads in the industry. Puget Systems has built its reputation on this work.
The R&D Lab
engages directly with the PC hardware ecosystem (component manufacturers and vendors) to qualify components and design the laptops, workstations, servers, and storage that meet the workflow needs the Performance Lab identifies.

This VP will not own Puget Labs on day one. The job starts with software and IT. But once that foundation is well in hand, leadership of Puget Labs is the intended growth path for this role, bringing the company's core differentiator under the same technology leadership. Candidates should be genuinely excited by that trajectory: this is ultimately a role that grows into stewarding what makes Puget Systems special.

Who You Are

A player-coach, permanently.
You are a strong hands-on engineer who still writes and reviews code, and you expect to keep doing so.
Experienced with inherited systems.
You've taken ownership of large, long-lived, lightly-documented codebases before (ideally from the original author) and you know how to handle that transition.
A builder of teams.
You have a track record of growing junior developers into strong ones, and of hiring well. You mentor others, even those not on your team.
Pragmatic about processes.
You know that process and documentation sets up a team for success, and you calibrate to company size.
Broad across software and IT.
You're credible leading both application development and IT/infrastructure/security for a mid-sized business.
A clear communicator with non-technical leaders.
You can explain tradeoffs, set expectations, and earn trust across sales, production, and operations teams whose daily work runs on your systems.
Financially accountable.
You've owned a department budget before and treat it as a real commitment, including planning annually, tracking monthly, and making tradeoffs transparently.

Qualifications

10+ years in software development and/or IT, including 3+ years leading a technology function as Director, VP, CTO, or Head of Engineering/IT.
Direct experience owning both software and IT for a mid-sized business (roughly 50–500 employees). We're looking for proof you've done this specific job, not a scaled-down version of a big-company role, and not a first step up from team lead.
A track record of maturing a technology organization: you can point to specific practices you established, systems you stabilized or replaced, and people who grew under your leadership.
Deep hands-on proficiency with the LAMP stack, which our internal platform is built on, plus working fluency with a modern JavaScript framework (we've tentatively standardized on Vue for new projects); WordPress and API-driven integration experience is a plus.
Prior ownership of a department budget.

Physical Requirements

Prolonged periods sitting at a desk and working on a computer.
Able to work from home or office.
Able to travel for trade shows and other activities.

Nice to Have

Experience in manufacturing, e-commerce, or configure-to-order businesses
Experience working directly with a founder/owner in a succession or transition capacity
Familiarity with ERP internal systems, whether homegrown or commercial
Experience building or managing data lakes, data pipelines, and BI reporting stacks
Experience meeting security requirements (e.g., customer security requirements, SOC2, NIST, or CMMC frameworks)

Why This Role Is Worth It

You'll inherit a genuinely interesting technical asset, a supportive founder who wants to hand it off well, a profitable and stable company with a strong reputation, and a team eager to grow. Your decisions will affect the entire company, and the role grows into stewardship of Puget Labs, who is the industry-respected source of our reputation. Few VP roles offer this much ownership with this little bureaucracy.

Oportun (Nasdaq: OPRT) is a mission-driven financial services company that puts its members' financial goals within reach. This inclusive culture is directly connected to our organization's performance and ability to fulfill our mission of delivering affordable credit to those left out of the financial mainstream. We celebrate and nurture our inclusive culture through our employee resource groups.

Position Overview

We are seeking a Senior Manager, Information Security Architecture & Engineering to serve as a key security leader within our organization. This role is responsible for defining and driving platform, application and data security, including designing and reinforcing secure-by-design principles, effective data protection and handling, identity and access management standards, and vulnerability management across the enterprise. Acting primarily as a second-line of defense, this leader ensures security best practices are embedded into our CI/CD, SDLC, data pipelines, and platform.

Beyond technical expertise, this role demands strong leadership to both manage a team of security experts, as well as drive initiatives across teams and functions. The ideal candidate will foster a culture of collaboration, continuous learning, and high performance, prioritizing kindness, integrity, and transparency in leadership. This individual will view security as a business enabler, creating services that empower developers and system owners to iterate rapidly while maintaining strong and pragmatic security controls.

What You'll Do

Define and maintain secure application and infrastructure architecture frameworks, ensuring security is built-in from the outset
Partner with engineering, DevOps, and technology teams to integrate security into SDLC, CI/CD, and data pipelines
Own and oversee the vulnerability management program, ensuring risk-based remediation across all technology assets
Enhance and scale an existing security design review service, providing structured security assessments for new and evolving systems and data
Advocate for security as a service, building tools and processes that streamline secure development and system operations
Act as a security advisor to engineering and technology operations, ensuring security aligns with business goals
Collaborate with the Security Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) team to align technical security requirements with regulatory and commercial requirements
Champion a security-first culture, ensuring technical execution teams understand security risks, standards and best practices

Who You Are / What You Bring

10+ years of experience in security architecture, application security, infrastructure security, or related domains
Strong background in cloud security (AWS, Azure, GCP), DevSecOps, and/or data security
Experience leading a globally distributed team across time zones which relies heavily on asynchronous working and collaboration methods
Experience leading and developing globally distributed security teams with a focus on professional growth and collaboration
Experience designing security controls for data flows and distributed computing environments
Hands-on expertise of secure software development practices, security testing methodologies, and threat modeling
Strong cross-functional leadership with the ability to communicate security risks effectively to engineering, IT, and business stakeholders
Experience of security frameworks and regulations (e.g., NIST CSF, PCI-DSS, GLBA)
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Security, or related field

Preferred Qualifications

Expertise in application security testing, threat modeling, bug bounty programs, and software security assessments
Expertise in identity & access management (IAM), encryption, authentication, logging, and monitoring architectures
Experience with GitHub, Wiz, Sentinel One and Okta
Security certifications (CISSP, CISM, OSCP, AWS Security Specialty, or similar)
Advanced degree in Computer Science, Information Security or related field

LineVision is hiring an operating executive who can turn grid intelligence software and hardware into the systems regulated utilities depend on to run their operations.

We are seeking a VP of Engineering
to own engineering delivery across our software and hardware organizations. You will run delivery of Nexus Core, our next-generation multi-tenant SaaS platform for dynamic line rating, as it moves past launch and into daily operations for a growing base of utility customers. You will also bring the engineering judgment behind the current wave of hardware evolution on our field-deployed sensor. If you want to build and run a development organization at pace across software and hardware, and be accountable for the commitments regulated utilities depend on, join us at LineVision
, Built In Boston Best Places to Work !

What will you do?

Core Responsibilities And Key Performance Objectives

Lead engineering delivery across Platform, Applications, Embedded Software, Data Science, and Hardware Engineering, with every director and manager in these functions reporting through this role.
Drive Nexus Core's ongoing release cadence, across multi-tenant SaaS and on-premise deployments for regulated, international customers.
Guide the field-deployed sensor fleet, including health monitoring, lifecycle management, and the next-generation sensor launch, bringing hardware design judgment to component and subsystem trade-offs.
Establish delivery standards and a reporting cadence across the org: milestone-level, on track or not, with a named owner for every commitment.
Represent engineering to the executive team and partner with Product, Sales, Customer Success, and Finance on delivery commitments, forecasting, and customer escalations.

Within the first 3 months:

Develop a working command of Nexus Core's architecture and release history, the sensor fleet's current state, and the org structure across all four functions.
Stand up a milestone-level reporting cadence with named owners across Platform, Applications, Data Science, and Hardware/Firmware.
Build working relationships with Product, Sales, Customer Success, and Finance leaders on delivery commitments and forecasting.

Within the first 6 months:

Run Nexus Core's release cadence against hard external commitments for existing SaaS and on-premise customers.
Drive the component and subsystem decisions for the next-generation sensor launch, working closely with the hardware/firmware manager.
Next-generation sensor design decisions are locked and moving through execution toward launch

Milestones within the first year:

Nexus Core is on a predictable release cadence that consistently meets external commitments across SaaS and on-premise deployments.
The org is staffed with strong managers and senior ICs across Platform, Applications, Data Science, and Hardware/Firmware.

How To Succeed In This Role

Key Competencies

Critical Thinking: Diagnose complex delivery, architecture, and hardware trade-offs across software and hardware. Push the organization toward evidence-based decisions over assumptions.
Taking Ownership: Own delivery outcomes for Nexus Core and the sensor fleet end to end. Hold every commitment to a named owner and a clear status.
Judgment & Decision Making: Weigh risk and opportunity across competing priorities in software and hardware delivery. Make the call, communicate it clearly, and stand behind it.
Stakeholder Management: Align Product, Sales, Customer Success, and Finance on delivery commitments and forecasts. Represent engineering credibly to the executive team.

Essential Skills

12+ years in engineering, with several years leading engineering organizations that shipped production software to external customers, preferably in industrial markets.
Track record delivering a multi-tenant SaaS platform from architecture through general availability, then running its ongoing release cadence against hard external commitments.
Experience running on-premise or privately deployed software for enterprise customers with strict security or compliance requirements.
Hands-on hardware design experience for industrial or field-deployed products, including environmental hardening and certifications (UL, CE, FCC, IP-rated enclosures).

What Sets The Best Candidates Apart

Startup experience ramping a company from 1-N.
NERC CIP or comparable regulated critical-infrastructure experience.
Personally built data products or analytics platforms, not just partnered with the team building them.
Grid intelligence or dynamic line rating domain experience, or direct hardware/firmware, embedded, or OTA background.

Reporting & Team Structure

Reports to the CTO.
Lead an organization of 35+ full-time leaders, engineers and contractors, spanning Platform, Applications, and Embedded Software, Data Science, and Hardware Engineering.
Collaborates closely with Product, Sales, Customer Success, and Finance.

What does joining LineVision mean for you?

Impact. Your talent, time, and energy will critically impact our success in delivering utilities with grid intelligence to enable affordable, reliable power.
Ownership. You will hold broad responsibilities with high autonomy and trust in a communicative, collaborative, and fast-paced environment.
Flexibility. You will be empowered to maintain work-life balance with trust-based PTO.
Real World Innovation. You will lead a motivated, high-performing team working with cutting edge, patented technology to help utilities meet the demands of an AI-powered future.

Who We Are…

LineVision is a grid-enhancing technology company enabling electric utilities to deliver affordable, reliable power and accelerate the electrification of the global economy. Our grid intelligence platform delivers the most accurate, network-wide dynamic line ratings and enables safer, more reliable grid operations with a combination of optical sensors and advanced environmental modeling. LineVision's global customer base includes eight of the ten largest US utilities, including National Grid, Southern Company, and Exelon.

We are LineVisionaries:
We are Innovators: We light the way with tenacious creativity and do good work.
We are Empowered: With high trust and high autonomy, the floor is yours, and the opportunity is ours.
We are Welcoming: Come as you are, our doors are open. We are better together.
We are Trusted Partners: We elevate our customer champions through shared thought leadership. We deliver on commitments.
We are All In: We are building a community of passionate individuals who want to dent the universe.

At LineVision there's no such thing as a "perfect" candidate. We are looking for exceptional people who want to make a positive impact through their work and facilitate an organization where everyone can thrive. So whatever background you bring with you, please apply if this role would make you excited to come to work every day.
Meet our team, and understand our mission: https://www.linevisioninc.com/about-us

Job Description

We have an exciting opportunity for a Sr Manager Security Operations & Engineering at UL Research Institutes and UL Standards & Engagement, based in our Evanston, Illinois, office.

The Senior Manager of Security Operations & Engineering leads and strengthens UL Research Institutes (ULRI) and UL Standards & Engagement (ULSE) security operations, ensuring effective prevention, detection, response, and recovery from cyber threats. This role provides strategic and operational oversight across incident response, threat detection, vulnerability management, and security tooling, while aligning efforts with enterprise risk and business goals.

A key partner to IT, Legal, and business teams, this position embeds security into core processes, translates strategy into measurable outcomes, and drives continuous improvement to maintain resilient, audit-ready, and business-aligned security operations.

UL Research Institutes and UL Standards & Engagement

At UL Research Institutes (ULRI) and UL Standards & Engagement (ULSE), we expand the boundaries of safety science to create a more secure and sustainable world. For more than a century, we have studied the unintended consequences of innovation, designed solutions to mitigate risk, created new safety standards and shared our findings with academia, scientists, manufacturers, and policymakers across industries. We identify critical safety and sustainability issues, asking the tough questions because we believe a safer world begins with knowledge.

What You’ll Learn And Achieve

As the Sr Manager Security Operations & Engineering, you will play a key role in the rapid growth of UL as you:

Drive the long-term strategy, roadmap, and operational execution of Security Operations & Engineering in alignment with ULRI and ULSE goals, objectives, enterprise risk priorities, and resilience commitments.
Lead and manage enterprise security operations, including incident response, threat detection, security monitoring, vulnerability management, and operational security engineering.
Own the end-to-end security incident lifecycle, ensuring timely detection, triage, containment, remediation, post-incident reviews, lessons learned, and executive reporting.
Lead the advancement of AI security monitoring, governance, and controls to protect enterprise data, secure internal and external AI use cases, and mitigate emerging AI-driven risks.
Oversee the enterprise vulnerability and exposure management program, including scanning, risk-based prioritization, remediation coordination, metrics, and executive-level reporting.
Drive the implementation, optimization, integration, and operational maturity of security tooling, including SIEM, EDR, MDR, CSPM, DSPM, CNAPP, vulnerability scanners, cloud security platforms, and related security technologies.
Establish and mature security operations processes, playbooks, runbooks, standard operating procedures, and repeatable workflows to improve operational consistency, response effectiveness, and measurable outcomes.
Partner with Identity, Infrastructure, Application, Cloud, and Architecture teams to improve security telemetry, embed security controls into enterprise environments, and strengthen visibility across systems, applications, and data.
Continue to mature Microsoft Purview capabilities, including eDiscovery, Insider Risk Management, Data Loss Prevention, Information Protection, and related data protection controls.
Oversee third-party MSSP security functions, vendor relationships, service provider performance, operational budgets, and annual forecasting for security operations.
Provide executive-level visibility, briefings, metrics, KPIs, dashboards, and risk-based insights to the CISO and senior leadership, including progress against NIST CSF v2 audit findings, compliance requirements, control validation, and enterprise risk reduction objectives.

What Makes You a Great Fit

While no one candidate will embody every quality, the successful candidate will bring many of the following professional competencies and personal attributes:

Ability to conduct comprehensive gap analysis across various business functions and IT systems. Skilled in identifying potential risks and vulnerabilities and developing effective risk mitigation plans and controls.
Strong leadership and people-management skills with the ability to build, mentor, and scale security operations teams.
Demonstrated ability to translate technical security events into clear, risk-based business impacts for executive audiences.
Deep understanding of security operations & engineering concepts, including incident response, threat intelligence, vulnerability management, and monitoring.
Proven experience driving operational maturity using recognized cybersecurity frameworks and best practices.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with a data-driven approach to decision-making.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including executive and board-level reporting.
Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced, evolving environment.
High degree of integrity, accountability, and professionalism.

Professional Education And Experience Requirements For The Role Include

Bachelor’s degree in Information Security, Computer Science, Information Technology etc. Master’s degree is preferred.
7 years of progressive experience in cybersecurity, with at least 3 years in a security operations leadership role.
Knowledge and experience working in Azure and AWS security settings.
Experience working on Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) and NIST SP800-171 v2 preferred but not required
Hands-on experience with security technologies such as SIEM, EDR, MDR, vulnerability management, and cloud security platforms.
Demonstrated experience leading incident response and vulnerability management programs in an enterprise environment.
Experience working in regulated or audit-driven environments is strongly preferred.
Relevant certifications (e.g., CISSP, CISM, GIAC, or similar) preferred but not required.

About UL Research Institutes And UL Standards & Engagement

UL Research Institutes and UL Standards & Engagement are nonprofit organizations dedicated to advancing safety science research through the discovery and application of scientific knowledge. We conduct rigorous independent research and analyze safety data, convene experts worldwide to address risks, share knowledge through safety education and public outreach initiatives, and develop standards to guide safe commercialization of evolving technologies. We foster communities of safety, from grassroots initiatives for neighborhoods to summits of world leaders. Our organization employs collaborative and scientific approaches with partners and stakeholders to drive innovation and progress toward improving safety, security, and sustainability, ultimately enhancing societal well-being.

To learn more, visit our websites UL.org and ULSE.org.
